segments.text: Thank you for calling the line for Bristol City Bus Tour.
This is a recorded message.
In about four minutes, we will provide you what you need to know about the tour.
Being one of the best cities to live in Britain, Bristol has attracted tourists from all over
the world for many years.
One of the best ways to get to know the city is to take the bus tour, which provides
It's a delightful viewing experience from one of our open-top buses.
The round-trip tour of the city includes five stops where passengers can get on and
off the bus.
The first stop is where many people arrive in the city, Bristol Temple Mead's railway
station, the oldest and largest in the city.
While waiting for the bus, visitors can enjoy the historical design of the station.
The next stop is the city's most iconic structure, the Clifton Suspension Bridge.
Along with beautiful pictures you might take here, adventurous and adrenaline-seeking tourists
can't miss the opportunity for a bungee jump.
However, you need to book in advance to do this.
Passing the bridge, the bus tour continues towards Bristol Zoo.
Here there's a variety of animals, ranging from small bugs to big gorillas, from flying
birds to swimming penguins.
For those who are interested in fancy clothes and big brands, the next stop is for you.
After leaving the zoo, the bus takes you to Cabot Circus, the biggest shopping mall in
the city.
Our advice is to go here in the morning when it is rather quiet.
It gets busy in the afternoons, especially in the summer.
The last stop is Bristol's Harbourside, where many restaurants and pubs are located.
The Bristol Museum and Art Gallery, which is a few minutes' walk away from the harbour,
is also a great place to spend time in.
